key_insight: Research agents propose worthwhile experiments, but evidence that their rankings improve which experiments to run remains limited.
engineering_relevance: Use research agents to generate experiment candidates, but validate their prioritization before committing compute or adopting costlier agent teams.
method: Six frontier models, working alone or in teams, proposed minimum viable experiments for seven recent NLP papers.
Agents set pass thresholds, forecast outcomes and rank experiments before execution.
A separate executor attempted every experiment, including last-ranked ones, and three model auditors judged results.
evidence_signal: Of 415 experiments, auditors judged 194 sound, valuable and new, with 73 also beyond the seed paper and non-obvious; agents’ top choices beat random selection but showed no demonstrated advantage over choosing the first-written experiment.
watch_item: Outcomes were judged by model auditors, and teams cost more without a clear overall improvement in proposal quality.
paper_title: rTaste: Do Research Agents Have Taste? Evaluating Early Stage Research Judgment
